sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is at 101 North Queen Street, Kinston, ZIP 28501. Mail goes to PO Box 3289, Kinston, 28502. The front desk is 252-559-6420, and email goes to lcrod@lenoircountync.gov.

Counter and recording hours are weekdays, 8:30am to 5:00pm. The same desk files maps, assumed names, notary oaths and military discharges, and issues birth, death and marriage records, so a seller who also needs a certified family record can ask for it on the same trip.

The office applies state recording law, so a Lenoir County deed follows the same ground rules as one filed anywhere else in North Carolina.

sections.h2: From signed deed to recorded deed
sections.html:
After the grantor signs before a notary, the paper goes to the Kinston office with payment. The deputy stamps the date and time, indexes the grantor and grantee names, and assigns the book and page that title searchers will use.

  1. Have your closing attorney prepare and notarize the deed.
  2. Send it with the page fee and excise tax, by hand, by mail to the PO box, or electronically.
  3. Collect the receipt and note the book and page.
  4. Check the index a few days later to confirm your name shows as grantor.

E-recording is available, and filers who want to enroll can call Simplifile at (801) 223-1046. At the counter a debit or credit card works, though the county adds a small usage fee. Vital records ordered by mail are different: the office wants cash or a money order, never a personal check, along with a stamped return envelope and a photocopy of the requester's picture ID.

Recording charges are set by the state, and the office posts its own fee sheet as a link on its Register of Deeds page. Call the office to confirm the current sheet before you file.

Selected statewide recording charges under G.S. 161-10
DocumentCharge
Standard instrument$26 buys the first 15 pages; each page beyond adds $4
Mortgage or deed of trust$64 runs through page 35; each page beyond adds $4
Paid-off loan releaseNo charge
Map or plat$21 a sheet
Certified copy$5 on page one plus $2 per added page
Nonstandard paper$25 on top of the usual fee

Clearing an old loan before a Kinston sale adds a little delay but no filing charge.

sections.h2: Excise tax on a Lenoir County deed
sections.html:
The tax is $1 per $500 block of price or value, and a partial block is billed as a whole one. G.S. 105-228.30 puts payment on the transferor, so it is the seller's cost, due in Kinston before the deed goes on the books.

The county keeps one share for its general fund and forwards the other to the state each month, after refunds and the county's retained allowance.

Most sellers never write a separate check. The closing attorney deducts the tax at settlement and delivers it with the deed, so it shows up as a line on the seller's side of the closing statement.

In North Carolina, G.S. 47-18 ranks competing claims by the moment they reach the county books. A buyer who holds only a signed deed can lose to a creditor or later purchaser whose paper was registered first.

That is why lenders want recording on closing day. A deed that sits in a briefcase over a weekend leaves a gap during which a new judgment or lien could attach ahead of it.

Options, leases longer than three years and first-refusal rights fall under the same rule. If your Kinston-area property has any such document, ask for a title search that looks for them before a closing date is set.

The Lenoir County Tax Department shares the building at 101 North Queen Street and answers at 252-527-7174. It lists, appraises and bills property, and it maintains the records that follow transfers. Real estate sits on a permanent listing system, so owners file only when something about the property changes. Mobile homes, boats, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles must be listed in January or draw a 10 percent late penalty.

September 1 is the due date, and January 6 starts a 2 percent charge followed by monthly interest of three-fourths of one percent. Under G.S. 105-355 the tax lien dates from the listing date, which keeps old balances on the parcel. Ask the tax office for a payoff number and have the attorney pay it out of proceeds at settlement.

Begin with the index itself. Ask the Register of Deeds what appears under your surname and under the seller before you, then follow up on any loan, easement or plat you did not expect.

  • Names on the latest recorded deed, including heirs if a prior owner has died.
  • A recorded release for every paid-off loan.
  • Any unpaid county bill or present-use deferral.
  • Whether you will file by paper or sign up for e-recording.
  • Excise tax and filing charges, so your net number is realistic.

For an inherited house, call the clerk of superior court about the estate steps before anyone signs, and order a certified death certificate from the Register of Deeds, which keeps those records.

sections.h2: Packing the envelope for a mailed deed
sections.html:
Some sellers in outlying parts of the county mail the deed rather than driving to Kinston. If you do, address it to PO Box 3289 and include the notarized original, a check for the page fee and the excise tax, and a note with a phone number in case the deputy has a question. A deed that comes back for a formatting problem costs you days, and the nonstandard paper fee of $25 applies if the pages do not meet state layout rules.

Electronic filing avoids most of this. Your attorney or title company submits the file, the office reviews it, and the recorded copy returns the same way.

The county seat is Kinston, with a population of 55,837 and 27,402 housing units. Owners live in 59.2 percent of homes, and the typical owner-held home is worth $120,500. Only 131 building permits were issued in 2025. With values near $120,500, a fixed recording fee takes a bigger bite out of a modest sale, so figure your net with it in mind.

sections.h2: A cash sale at the Kinston counter
sections.html:
A cash buyer can shorten the path to closing, but the recording steps are the same as for any other sale. The deed is still signed before a notary, the seller's excise tax is still paid, and the file still goes to 101 North Queen Street by hand, by mail or electronically. What a cash sale removes is the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which often cause the delays.

If liens or back taxes sit on the house, the payoff letters are what you need to gather. A release of a paid-off mortgage costs nothing to record, so the cost of clearing the title is mostly the time it takes the lender to send the paperwork.

faqs.q: What are the office hours at the Lenoir County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8:30am to 5:00pm at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston. Call 252-559-6420 or write to PO Box 3289, Kinston, NC 28502.

faqs.q: Is e-recording available through Lenoir County?
faqs.a: Yes. Simplifile, at (801) 223-1046, handles enrollment. Ask your closing attorney whether the firm already files this way.

faqs.q: Who owes the excise tax on a Lenoir County deed?
faqs.a: The seller owes it, as transferor, before recording. The tax is $1 per $500 of value, with any part of a block counted whole, and the attorney normally subtracts it at settlement.

faqs.q: Do I pay to record a mortgage release in Lenoir County?
faqs.a: No. Recording a release of a mortgage or deed of trust is free under G.S. 161-10, so ask your lender to send it to the Kinston office after payoff.

faqs.q: How do I learn what property tax is due on a Lenoir County house?
faqs.a: Phone the tax department at 252-527-7174. Bills fall due September 1, interest begins January 6, and your attorney can pay the balance from sale proceeds.
